common_name: Kong Lime Sprite Coleus (Giant Chartreuse-and-Mahogany Shade Coleus)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants after all frost danger has passed into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; the oversized quilted leaves scorch quickly in direct sun.

directions: Grow in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, since Kong Lime Sprite's exceptionally large, quilted leaves bleach and burn in strong sun. Each leaf carries a bright lime-green field with deep mahogany-red veining and a contrasting maroon center, giving the plant strong textural presence at a scale most coleus can't match. Its fast, mounding growth fills shaded beds and large containers quickly, pairing well with hostas and ferns as a bold foliage anchor. Pinch flower spikes and growing tips regularly to keep the plant full and to prevent it from stretching and thinning with age.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company — Kong coleus series notes

common_name: ColorBlaze Wicked Witch Coleus (Ruffled Chocolate-Burgundy Chartreuse-Edged Coleus)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil; Wicked Witch tolerates everything from full sun to full shade and holds its color without scorching or fading.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil anywhere from full sun to full shade, since this ColorBlaze selection is bred for wide light tolerance without losing color intensity. Deeply ruffled, near-black chocolate-burgundy leaves are rimmed in a narrow chartreuse edge, creating strong contrast that reads well from a distance in mixed borders and large containers. It is exceptionally late to flower, so foliage color stays fresh and undisturbed by bloom spikes for most of the season, extending garden performance into fall. Pinch tips after transplanting to encourage branching, and shear lightly if plants become leggy in the heat of midsummer.
sources: Proven Winners — ColorBlaze Wicked Witch plant profile

common_name: Main Street Beale Street Coleus (AAS-Winning Sun-Tolerant True Red Coleus)

planting.note: Set out container plants after the last frost in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Beale Street was the first coleus ever named an AAS Ornamental Winner, prized for holding pure red color without scorching in hot sun.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil anywhere from full sun to full shade; unlike many red coleus, Beale Street's solid red foliage resists the bleaching, flecking, and scorch that typically appear on true-red cultivars grown in strong sun. Its compact, uniform, well-branched habit was bred for consistent performance across climates, making it reliable for mass bedding as well as containers. The 2020 All-America Selections Ornamental award recognized it as the first coleus ever to win the trial, based on outstanding weather tolerance and season-long color. Pinch young plants to encourage branching and remove flower spikes as they form to keep energy in the foliage.
sources: All-America Selections — 2020 AAS Ornamental Award Winner

common_name: Main Street Rodeo Drive Coleus (Bright Green Purple-Veined Sun-Tolerant Coleus)

planting.note: Set out container plants after the last frost in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Rodeo Drive's toothy bright green leaves are outlined in dark purple veining and a contrasting purple edge.

directions: Grow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, where this compact Main Street selection holds a tight, uniform habit well suited to pots and edging. Sharply toothed, scalloped bright green leaves are traced with dark purple veins and rimmed in a matching purple edge, giving the foliage a lacy, high-contrast look distinct from solid-colored coleus. Its small stature and weather-tolerant breeding keep it tidy in beds and mixed containers without frequent shearing. Pinch tips at planting to encourage branching and remove any flower spikes promptly to keep the plant compact and full of color.
sources: Dümmen Orange Main Street coleus series notes

common_name: FlameThrower Salsa Roja Coleus (Serrated Burgundy-Red Sun Coleus)

planting.note: Plant after all danger of frost in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Salsa Roja carries deeply serrated burgundy-red leaves on an upright, mounding plant that flowers very late if at all.

directions: Plant in well-drained garden soil or containers in full sun to light shade, where this FlameThrower series selection develops its deepest, most saturated color. Narrow, sharply serrated leaves in solid burgundy-red give the plant a spiky, fine-textured look that stands apart from broader-leaved coleus, and its upright, mounding habit holds shape well through the heat of summer. Bred as a true sun coleus, it resists the stretch and fade many shade-adapted cultivars show in strong light, and it is late to never flowering, so color holds without regular deadheading. Pinch stem tips after planting to build a fuller, more branched frame.
sources: Ball FloraPlant — FlameThrower coleus series notes

common_name: ColorBlaze Royale Apple Brandy Coleus (Burgundy-Maroon Chartreuse-Trimmed Coleus)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed in slightly acidic, well-drained soil kept evenly moist; Apple Brandy tolerates full sun to full shade and holds its bicolor foliage without scorching.

directions: Grow in evenly moist, well-drained soil with a slightly acidic to neutral pH, in exposures ranging from full sun to full shade. Deep burgundy-maroon leaves are trimmed in a narrow lime-green to yellow edge, and the well-branched, upright habit gives it good presence as a thriller in mixed containers or massed in a border. Like other ColorBlaze selections it is bred to flower very late or not at all, keeping foliage color the season-long focus rather than bloom spikes. Pinch young plants to encourage branching and water deeply during hot, dry stretches, since consistent moisture keeps the large leaves from wilting.
sources: Proven Winners — ColorBlaze Royale Apple Brandy plant profile
